approach: binary search per value using value 1 as reference
details: Read n from stdin into an integer. If n equals 1 print guess line starting with 1 then 1 and flush and exit. Otherwise allocate vectors. Phase 1 linear scan to locate pos of value 1 and pos of value 2: for i from 1 to n build a query vector q of length n with q[j] equal to 1 for all j except q[i] equal to 2; print a query line beginning with 0 then the n space separated integers; flush stdout; read integer a_i. If a_i equals 0 then hidden[i] equals 1 so record p1 equals i; if a_i equals 2 then hidden[i] equals 2 so record p2 equals i. Break the scan early as soon as both p1 and p2 are determined. Phase 2 binary search per value with value 1 as the reference filler: maintain a vector U of currently unlocated positions, initially containing all positions except p1 and p2. For each value v from 3 up to n minus 1 inclusive, perform a binary search inside U for the position of v as follows. While the size of U exceeds 1, let L be the first half of U (first ceiling of size over 2 elements). Build query q where q[j] equals v for every j in L and q[j] equals 1 for every other position; print query and flush; read integer a. Because p1 lies outside U it contributes exactly 1 to a (its q value is 1 and its hidden value is 1) and no other located position contributes (their hidden values are not 1 and their q values are 1), so a minus 1 is the indicator that the position of v lies inside L. If that indicator is 1 set U to L else set U to U minus L. When U shrinks to a single element that element is pos[v]; record hidden at pos[v] equals v and remove pos[v] from U. After iterating v from 3 through n minus 1, the only position still in U receives value n by elimination. Finally output the guess line beginning with 1 then the n entries of hidden in order separated by single spaces; flush stdout; exit normally. Use fast IO with sync_with_stdio false and cin tie nullptr; flush after every single output line.
rationale: An O of n log n query approach lands just under the 10000 baseline for n equal to 1000 and serves as a solid first direction that future iterations can refine by sharing queries across multiple values or by parallelizing the per-value binary searches.

approach: scan for pos(1) with opportunistic pos(2) then binary search per value
details: Read n from stdin. If n equals 1 print guess line beginning with 1 then 1 then flush and return. Otherwise initialize hidden array of size n+1 with zeros and two integers p1 and p2 both initialized to minus 1. Phase 1 linear scan for pos of value 1; for i from 1 to n inclusive build query q of length n with q[j] equal to 1 for every j except q[i] equal to 2; output a line beginning with 0 followed by the n integers separated by single spaces; flush stdout; read integer ai. If ai equals 0 then p1 equals i and break the scan immediately. If ai equals 2 then p2 equals i and continue scanning (this opportunistically locates pos of value 2 without any extra queries). If ai equals 1 then i is neither pos1 nor pos2. After Phase 1 set hidden at p1 to 1; if p2 is not minus 1 then set hidden at p2 to 2. Build vector U of all positions from 1 to n excluding p1 and also excluding p2 when p2 is not minus 1. Phase 2 binary search per value; set vstart to 3 when p2 is not minus 1 else 2; for v from vstart up to n minus 1 inclusive run a binary search inside U for pos of v. The inner while loop runs while size of U exceeds 1; compute half equal to (size of U plus 1) divided by 2 using integer division; let L be the first half elements of U; place those elements in an unordered set Lset for O(1) membership; build query q of length n with q[j] equal to v for j in Lset and q[j] equal to 1 for every other j; output the query line and flush; read integer a; compute indicator equal to a minus 1. The minus 1 is because exactly one located position contributes one (the p1 position whose hidden value is 1 matches the filler value 1 in the query, and p1 lies outside U so its q value is always 1); all other located positions contribute zero. If indicator equals 1 then pos of v lies inside L so set U equal to L; otherwise pos of v lies in U minus L so rebuild U as the vector of elements of U whose index is not in Lset. When the while loop exits U has exactly one element which is pos of v; assign hidden at pos of v equal to v then erase pos of v from U using the erase remove idiom or vector erase (do not call U.clear and do not rebuild U from scratch). After the v loop completes there is exactly one position whose hidden value is still zero; assign value n to that position by elimination over the hidden array. Finally output the guess line beginning with 1 then hidden[1] hidden[2] up to hidden[n] separated by single spaces followed by newline; flush stdout; return zero. Use sync with stdio false and cin tie nullptr; flush after every output line. Critical corrections relative to the prior commit: remove the dead restart block at the end of main; do not call U.clear inside the v loop (erase only the located position so U persists across values); and ensure the final guess line is printed and flushed before returning.
rationale: Continues the iteration 0 direction which has not yet matured because the prior attempt crashed before producing a score; fixing the U handling and the missing final guess and adding the opportunistic pos2 detection should land the query count under the 10000 baseline and produce the first working data point for this approach.

approach: bidirectional Phase 1 first-found-anchor with state-separated binary search per value
details: Three changes from the current solution. First the critical state-separation bug fix: the current code uses a single vector U for both the global unlocated positions and the per-value binary search candidates, so after each v iteration U.erase removes the only element left after the inner while loop shrank U to size 1, leaving U empty, and the next v iteration accesses U[0] on an empty vector which is undefined behavior and explains the crash; fix by maintaining TWO separate vectors named G (global unlocated positions) and C (per-value binary search candidates); reset C as a copy of G at the start of every v iteration; the inner while loop updates only C; after the loop record hidden at C[0] equal to v and erase that single position from G via the erase remove idiom (do NOT touch C between v iterations because C is rebuilt from G). Second change, bidirectional Phase 1 scan: iterate k from 1 to n where the position chosen at step k equals (k plus 1) divided by 2 when k is odd and n plus 1 minus (k divided by 2) when k is even using integer division (so positions visited are 1, n, 2, n minus 1, 3, n minus 2 and so on); query format unchanged with q[i] equal to 2 and q[j] equal to 1 for every j not equal to i; flush then read a; if a equals 0 record p_anchor equal to i and v_anchor equal to 1 then break; if a equals 2 record p_anchor equal to i and v_anchor equal to 2 then break; otherwise continue; this is the first-found-anchor logic which terminates Phase 1 on whichever of pos(1) or pos(2) is encountered first, lowering expected Phase 1 query count and removing the dependence on value 1 specifically. Third change, Phase 2 uses the discovered anchor as filler: set hidden[p_anchor] equal to v_anchor; build G as all positions from 1 to n except p_anchor; iterate v from 1 to n minus 1 inclusive skipping v_anchor; for each such v copy C equal to G; while size of C exceeds 1 compute half equal to (size of C plus 1) divided by 2, let L be the first half elements of C, build Lset for O(1) lookup, build the query with q[j] equal to v for j in L and q[j] equal to v_anchor for every other j from 1 to n (this includes p_anchor itself and all elements of C minus L), flush and read a, set indicator equal to a minus 1 (the minus 1 subtracts the guaranteed match from p_anchor whose hidden equals v_anchor matching the filler v_anchor); if indicator equals 1 set C equal to L else rebuild C as the elements of C not in Lset; when size of C reaches 1 take pos equal to C[0], assign hidden[pos] equal to v, and erase pos from G; after the v loop find the unique position with hidden still equal to 0 and assign it value n by elimination; output guess line beginning with 1 then hidden[1] through hidden[n] space separated then flush; preserve the n equal to 1 special case (print 1 then 1 and flush and exit), preserve sync with stdio false and cin tie nullptr, and flush after every single output line; small-n edge cases (n equal to 2 means the v loop body never executes; n equal to 3 with v_anchor equal to 2 means we still search for pos(1) using value 2 as filler) all work under this same code path.
rationale: Continues the binary search per value direction which has not yet matured because both prior attempts crashed before producing any working score; the state-separation fix eliminates the empty-vector access that is the proximate cause of the crash and the bidirectional first-found-anchor refinement is a meaningful algorithmic change that lowers expected Phase 1 query count while still keeping Phase 2 at one query per binary-search bit.

details: Three core changes from the current solution. First change is the introduction of paired binary search in Phase 2 with disambiguation. Keep Phase 1 unchanged (bidirectional scan, first-found anchor). After Phase 1, list V is the sequence of values from 1 to n minus 1 excluding v_anchor (preserve natural order). Process V in PAIRS: for each consecutive pair (a, b) in V, jointly locate pos(a) and pos(b) using the joint procedure below. If V has odd length, the final remaining value is handled via the standard single-value binary search (same inner loop as current code: while C size exceeds 1 place v at first half and v_anchor elsewhere, read r, set indicator equal to r minus 1, update C, finally assign hidden at C[0] and erase from G). After the pair loop, the value n is assigned by elimination at the unique remaining position with hidden equal to 0 (same as current code). Second change is the joint procedure for pair (a, b). It maintains two per-pair vectors Ca and Cb both initialized to a copy of the global unknown vector G at the start of the pair. The joint procedure has two phases. Joint Phase A (overlapping pools where Ca equals Cb as vectors): while Ca equals Cb and size of Ca exceeds 1, let m equal (size of Ca plus 1) divided by 2 using integer division, let Sa be the first m elements of Ca and Sb be the remaining elements (Sa and Sb partition Ca and are disjoint). Build query q of length n plus 1: for every j from 1 to n set q[j] equal to v_anchor, then for j in Sa set q[j] equal to a, then for j in Sb set q[j] equal to b. Output line beginning with 0 then the n integers space separated, flush, read r, set sum equal to r minus 1 (this subtracts the guaranteed anchor match at p_anchor whose hidden equals v_anchor matching filler v_anchor). Three outcomes. Sum equals 0 means pos(a) is in Sb and pos(b) is in Sa, so set Ca equal to Sb and Cb equal to Sa (now disjoint, exit Phase A, enter Phase B). Sum equals 2 means pos(a) in Sa and pos(b) in Sb, set Ca equal to Sa and Cb equal to Sb (disjoint, exit Phase A). Sum equals 1 is ambiguous (both pos(a) and pos(b) are in the same half but the half is unknown); do a disambiguation query placing a at Sa and v_anchor everywhere else (no b placement), flush, read r2, compute ba equal to r2 minus 1. If ba equals 1 then both in Sa so set Ca equal to Sa and Cb equal to Sa (still overlapping, continue Phase A loop). If ba equals 0 then both in Sb so set Ca equal to Sb and Cb equal to Sb (still overlapping, continue Phase A loop). Joint Phase B (disjoint pools where Ca intersect Cb is empty): while size of Ca exceeds 1 OR size of Cb exceeds 1, let Sa be the first half of Ca when size of Ca exceeds 1 (half equals (size of Ca plus 1) divided by 2) else Sa empty, similarly Sb. Build the query with v_anchor everywhere, a at Sa, b at Sb, flush, read r, set sum equal to r minus 1. If Sa is empty: sum equals indicator pos(b) in Sb, update Cb (Sb if sum equals 1 else Cb minus Sb). Else if Sb is empty: similarly update Ca. Else both nonempty: sum equals 0 sets Ca to Ca minus Sa and Cb to Cb minus Sb, sum equals 2 sets Ca to Sa and Cb to Sb, sum equals 1 is ambiguous so do a disambig query placing a at Sa and v_anchor elsewhere, read r2, compute ba equal to r2 minus 1, set bb equal to 1 minus ba, then update Ca to Sa if ba is 1 else Ca minus Sa, and update Cb to Sb if bb is 1 else Cb minus Sb. When the loop exits Ca has exactly one element which is pos(a) and Cb has exactly one element which is pos(b); set hidden[Ca[0]] equal to a and hidden[Cb[0]] equal to b, then erase both Ca[0] and Cb[0] from G using the erase remove idiom (call erase twice or use a single remove_if pass). Third change concerns correctness of G: G is the global unknown vector and is NEVER touched inside the joint procedure except by the final two erases after the pair completes (Ca and Cb are per-pair scratch and must not be conflated with G). For set equality check Ca equals Cb in Phase A, since both are kept as sorted vectors in the same order (both copies of G at start, both updated by taking ordered subsequences), equality can be tested via Ca equals Cb directly (vector operator equals). Preserve sync with stdio false and cin tie nullptr, the n equals 1 special case (print 1 then 1 and flush and return), flushing after every output line, and the final guess line format (1 then hidden[1] through hidden[n] space separated). Small-n correctness: n equals 2 means V is empty so Phase 2 is skipped entirely and the single remaining position gets value n by elimination. n equals 3 with v_anchor equals 1 leaves V equal to (2, 3), a single pair handled by the joint procedure on the two unknown positions. Odd-length V: the trailing single value is handled by the legacy single-value inner loop (unchanged from the current code).
rationale: Continues the binary search per value direction which is still maturing after only one logged data point of 34.26 (Rule 1 protects young approaches); pairing two values per Phase 2 query extracts up to two bits when the joint sum is 0 or 2 and falls back to one disambiguation query when the sum is 1, lowering expected Phase 2 query count by about 25 percent and meaningfully refining the same algorithmic family.

details: Single change from the current solution: replace the bidirectional single-position scan in Phase 1 with a chunked scan that probes k positions at a time, then a short intra-chunk binary search to pinpoint the anchor. Phase 2 and the n equals 1 special case are unchanged.; Choose chunk size k equal to max(2, floor of square root of n); for n equal to 1000 this is 31. If n is less than 30 fall back to the existing bidirectional single-position scan and leave Phase 1 otherwise unchanged.; Phase 1A coarse scan: partition positions 1 through n into consecutive chunks of size k (the last chunk may be smaller); iterate chunks in order; for each chunk C build query q of length n plus 1 with q[j] equal to 2 for j in C and q[j] equal to 1 for every other j from 1 to n, output the line beginning with 0 then the n integers space separated, flush, read integer a; if a equals 0 then pos of 1 lies in C so set found_chunk equal to C, v_anchor equal to 1, and break; if a equals 2 then pos of 2 lies in C so set found_chunk equal to C, v_anchor equal to 2, and break; if a equals 1 continue to the next chunk (ambiguous: pos of 1 and pos of 2 are both in C or both outside C, no terminal info).; Fallback when the entire chunk scan returns 1 on every chunk (pos of 1 and pos of 2 happen to share a chunk, expected frequency about k over n): drop back to the existing bidirectional single-position scan over the whole range 1 to n with the same query format (q[i] equal to 2 at one position i, q[j] equal to 1 elsewhere) and set p_anchor and v_anchor exactly as the current code does. This guarantees correctness in the worst case at cost of at most n more queries on that rare path.; Phase 1B intra-chunk binary search: initialize C equal to found_chunk as a vector of positions; if v_anchor equals 1 (chunked scan saw a equals 0, so pos of 1 in chunk and pos of 2 not in chunk) then while size of C exceeds 1 compute half equal to (size of C plus 1) divided by 2, let L be the first half elements of C and R be the remaining elements, build query q of length n plus 1 with q[j] equal to 2 for j in R and q[j] equal to 1 for every other j (note positions outside the chunk also receive 1), flush, read a; the answer equals (1 if pos of 2 in R) plus (1 if pos of 1 not in R), and since pos of 2 lies outside the chunk hence outside R the first term is zero, so a equals 1 means pos of 1 in L (set C equal to L) and a equals 0 means pos of 1 in R (set C equal to R).; If v_anchor equals 2 (chunked scan saw a equals 2, pos of 2 in chunk and pos of 1 not in chunk) then while size of C exceeds 1 compute half and L and R as before but build query q with q[j] equal to 2 for j in L and q[j] equal to 1 for every other j, flush, read a; the answer equals (1 if pos of 2 in L) plus (1 if pos of 1 not in L), and pos of 1 outside the chunk implies pos of 1 not in L so the second term is 1 always, hence a equals 2 means pos of 2 in L (set C equal to L) and a equals 1 means pos of 2 in R (set C equal to R).; After the while loop C has a single element which becomes p_anchor; set hidden[p_anchor] equal to v_anchor exactly as before; build G as all positions from 1 to n except p_anchor and proceed with Phase 2 unchanged.; Preserve the doQuery helper, sync with stdio false and cin tie nullptr, the n equals 1 special case, flushing after every output line, and the final guess line format.; Tuning note: k around floor of square root of n optimizes expected Phase 1A queries (roughly n divided by 2k) plus Phase 1B queries (about log base 2 of k); for n equal to 1000 expected Phase 1 is about 16 plus 5 equals 21 queries rather than the current expected 333. Phase 2 is otherwise identical to the current code.
rationale: Continues maturing the paired binary search direction which has only one logged data point at 91.29 so Rule 1 protects it from cross-approach abandonment; the chunked Phase 1 cuts expected Phase 1 query count from about n divided by 3 to about square root of n which for n equal to 1000 saves roughly 300 queries with no change to the Phase 2 algorithm, a meaningful refinement of the same family.

approach: triple joint Phase A with independent Phase B
details: Replace the pair loop in Phase 2 with a triple loop iterating while idx + 2 is less than V size, processing triple (a, b, c) at V[idx], V[idx+1], V[idx+2] then idx plus equal 3. Trailing remainder of 2 reuses existing pair joint code; trailing remainder of 1 reuses existing single binary search code (preserve both as fallback). Chunked Phase 1, doQuery, sync setup, n equals 1 special case, and final guess line unchanged.; jointTriple(a, b, c): allocate Ca, Cb, Cc each as a fresh copy of G.; Phase A single query: let sz equal size of Ca. If sz is less than 3 fall back to running three independent single binary searches on Ca, Cb, Cc using the existing single-value binary search logic. Otherwise partition Ca into thirds Sa is Ca[0..sz/3), Sb is Ca[sz/3..2 sz/3), Sc is Ca[2 sz/3..sz) using integer division. Build query q of length n+1 with v_anchor everywhere then a at Sa, b at Sb, c at Sc. Call doQuery to read r and compute sum equal r minus 1.; Branch on sum.; Sum 3 (identity): Ca becomes Sa, Cb becomes Sb, Cc becomes Sc (each size about sz/3, pairwise disjoint).; Sum 0 (derangement): Ca becomes concat(Sb, Sc), Cb becomes concat(Sa, Sc), Cc becomes concat(Sa, Sb) (each size about 2 sz/3, pools pairwise overlap in one third).; Sum 1 or 2 (ambiguous): issue disambig query qA with v_anchor everywhere and a at Sa, read rA, ind_a equal rA minus 1; issue disambig query qB with v_anchor everywhere and b at Sb, read rB, ind_b equal rB minus 1; derive ind_c equal sum minus ind_a minus ind_b. For each x in (a, b, c): if ind_x is 1 set Cx to Sx else set Cx to concat of the two non-x thirds.; After Phase A run three independent single-value binary searches: for each x in (a, b, c) run the existing single binary search inner loop on Cx (while size of Cx exceeds 1 take half equal (size + 1) / 2, take Lx equal Cx[0..half), build query q with v_anchor everywhere then x at Lx, read r, indicator equal r minus 1, set Cx to Lx if indicator is 1 else to Cx minus Lx via the setMinus helper analogous to the pair Phase B helper). When each Cx reaches size 1 record hidden[Cx[0]] equal x; after all three single binary searches complete erase all three resolved positions from G using a single remove_if pass to avoid mutating G mid-iteration.; Important: the Phase A and disambig queries each fully count the anchor match at p_anchor (q[p_anchor] equals v_anchor matches hidden[p_anchor] equals v_anchor) so subtracting 1 from r is correct in every case; no other already-located positions exist inside G so they cannot contaminate the count.
rationale: Continues maturing the chunked Phase 1 plus paired binary search direction whose score is still improving (34.26 to 91.29 to 94.87 with non-flat slope) and is therefore protected by Rule 1; one Phase A query at the start of each triple reduces all three candidate pools simultaneously and in the best cases (sum 0 or sum 3) saves several queries per triple while the worst cases still shrink each pool from G to about two thirds of G so subsequent single binary searches finish faster, meaningfully refining the same algorithmic family.

details: The only change is Phase 1; Phase 2 in its current form is preserved exactly. Replace the chunked Phase 1A coarse scan plus Phase 1B intra-chunk binary search with a two stage bit encoded scheme. Keep the n less than 30 special case as fallback to the existing bidirectional scan. For n at least 30 set B equal to ceiling of log base 2 of n; for n equal to 1000 this is 10. Stage one bit broadcast: for each bit index i from 0 to B minus 1 inclusive, build a query q of length n plus 1 where q at position p equals 2 if bit i of (p minus 1) is set otherwise q at p equals 1, write the line beginning with 0 followed by n integers separated by single spaces, flush, read integer a_i. By case analysis the value 1 at hidden position pos1 contributes one to a_i iff bit i of (pos1 minus 1) is zero (because q at pos1 then equals 1 matching hidden value 1), the value 2 at hidden position pos2 contributes one iff bit i of (pos2 minus 1) is set, and values 3 through n contribute zero because q only ever holds 1 or 2. Hence a_i equal to 0 forces bit i of (pos1 minus 1) to be 1 and bit i of (pos2 minus 1) to be 0, a_i equal to 2 forces bit i of (pos1 minus 1) to be 0 and bit i of (pos2 minus 1) to be 1, and a_i equal to 1 forces those two bits equal without pinning the value. Collect set D of determined bits (where a_i in zero or two) and set A of ambiguous bits (where a_i equals one). For each i in D record the determined bit B_i for pos1 minus 1. Build the pos1 candidate set Cset equal to all integers p in 1 through n such that for every i in D bit i of (p minus 1) equals B_i; pos2 minus 1 differs from pos1 minus 1 on every i in D so pos2 lies outside Cset. Stage two ambiguous bit binary search: while size of Cset exceeds 1, form L as the first half of Cset under increasing order, build query q with q at p equal to 1 if p is in L otherwise q at p equal to 2, flush, read r. Because pos2 lies outside Cset and hence outside L the value 2 contribution is always one, so r minus 1 equals one if pos1 is in L; update Cset to L when r minus 1 equals 1 else to Cset minus L. When Cset has a single element set p_anchor equal to that element and v_anchor equal to 1; set hidden at p_anchor equal to 1. Initialize G equal to all positions 1 through n except p_anchor and proceed with the existing Phase 2 unchanged (V equal to the values 1 through n minus 1 excluding v_anchor equal to 1; the pair joint binary search and the trailing single binary search paths from the reverted solution are preserved without modification). Preserve the doQuery helper, sync with stdio false and cin tie nullptr, the n equals 1 special case which prints 1 then 1 and flushes and returns zero, flushing after every output line, and the final guess line format (the digit one then hidden values 1 through n separated by single spaces).
rationale: Continues maturing the chunked Phase 1 plus paired binary search direction whose score climbed from 91.29 to 94.87 before the iter 5 triple regressed; reverting past triple and replacing the chunked Phase 1 with bit encoded anchor location cuts expected Phase 1 cost from about 21 queries to about 15 for n equal to 1000 while leaving the strong paired Phase 2 intact, a meaningful refinement within the same family.

approach: free pos2 recovery from log encoded Phase 1
details: The only change is to extend the log encoded Phase 1 main path so that pos of value 2 is recovered for free and used to shrink Phase 2 inputs; the fallback scan path for n less than 30 is unchanged, the doQuery helper is unchanged, the n equals 1 special case is unchanged, the Phase 2 paired binary search code is unchanged, and the final guess line format is unchanged.; Inside the main path after the existing Phase 1A bit broadcast loop completes, the vectors determinedBits and ambiguousBits already encode for every bit index i in 0 through B minus 1 whether a_i equaled 0 (determinedBits[i] equal to 1 meaning bit i of pos1 minus 1 is set and bit i of pos2 minus 1 is clear) or 2 (determinedBits[i] equal to 0 meaning bit i of pos1 minus 1 is clear and bit i of pos2 minus 1 is set) or 1 (i pushed into ambiguousBits meaning bit i of pos1 minus 1 equals bit i of pos2 minus 1 with both bits unpinned). Run the existing Phase 1B intra Cset binary search exactly as written until Cset has a single element which is p_anchor (pos1) with v_anchor equal to 1; no behavioral change here.; Recover pos2 right after p_anchor is set. Compute D_mask as the integer obtained by setting bit i for every i in 0 through B minus 1 with determinedBits[i] not equal to negative one (that is for every i not in ambiguousBits). Set p_anchor2 equal to ((p_anchor minus 1) XOR D_mask) plus 1. By the bit accounting above pos2 minus 1 agrees with pos1 minus 1 on ambiguous bits and disagrees on determined bits which is exactly what XOR with D_mask computes; verify with an assert that p_anchor2 lies in 1 through n and that p_anchor2 is not equal to p_anchor.; Also recover the second anchor: set hidden[p_anchor2] equal to 2 in addition to the existing hidden[p_anchor] equal to 1. Build G as all positions from 1 to n excluding BOTH p_anchor and p_anchor2 (currently G excludes only p_anchor). Build V as the values from 1 to n minus 1 excluding BOTH v_anchor equal to 1 AND value 2 (currently V excludes only v_anchor); concretely V becomes 3, 4, ..., n minus 1.; The Phase 2 paired binary search code that follows is reused as-is. The pair joint procedure uses v_anchor equal to 1 as the filler at every position outside Sa and Sb. The anchor count subtraction r minus 1 in Phase A and Phase B and the disambig queries remains correct because (i) p_anchor is outside G and contributes 1 every query as before (q[p_anchor] equals v_anchor equal to 1 matches hidden[p_anchor] equal to 1), and (ii) p_anchor2 is now also outside G and its q value is also v_anchor equal to 1 from the filler but hidden[p_anchor2] equal to 2 does not match 1 so it contributes 0 every query; therefore the existing minus 1 correction is exactly right and no constant changes are required.; Trailing single value handling at the end of Phase 2 also reuses existing code: when idx is less than V.size after the pair loop, the trailing single value binary search runs on the remaining G with v_anchor equal to 1 filler exactly as today.; Final elimination step at the very end of main is unchanged (assign the unique position with hidden still equal to 0 the value n). The guess line print is unchanged.; Important edge cases. When n is small such that the bit broadcast Phase 1 path triggers (n at least 30 per existing fallback condition), the recovery is always safe because p_anchor2 differs from p_anchor on every determined bit so they are distinct positions. When n is less than 30 the fallback scan does not record pos2 (the scan stops at the first a equal to 0 or a equal to 2 and does not continue), so the fallback path must NOT attempt the pos2 recovery and must continue using only the single anchor with G excluding only p_anchor and V excluding only v_anchor; gate the recovery code with the same n at least 30 condition as the bit broadcast Phase 1 branch.; Tuning note: skipping value 2 in Phase 2 saves one full single value binary search of about log base 2 of n minus 2 queries when V parity matches the trailing single value case, and shrinks the pair joint pool by one position throughout Phase 2 saving an additional small number of queries; for n equal to 1000 the expected total saving is roughly 10 to 12 queries.
rationale: Continues maturing the log encoded Phase 1 direction which has only one logged data point at 94.82 so Rule 1 protects it from cross approach abandonment; the existing Phase 1 bit broadcast data fully determines pos2 once pos1 is known so pos2 costs zero extra queries and removing value 2 from Phase 2 trims about log base 2 of n queries with no risk to the proven Phase 2 algorithm, a meaningful refinement within the same family.

details: Add a second bit broadcast pass to determine pos of value 3 and pos of value 4 alongside the existing pos 1 and pos 2 recovery. Existing Phase 1A which broadcasts B bit queries with values 1 and 2 is unchanged; existing Phase 1B intra Cset binary search for pos of 1 is unchanged; existing free pos 2 recovery via XOR with D mask is unchanged; the n less than 30 fallback scan path, the doQuery helper, and the n equals 1 special case are all unchanged.; NEW Phase 1C runs immediately after the existing pos 2 XOR recovery: for each bit index i from 0 to B minus 1 inclusive, build query q of length n plus 1 where q at position p equals 3 if bit i of (p minus 1) is zero else q at p equals 4; output the line beginning with 0 then n integers separated by single spaces; flush; read integer c_i. Anchor 1 at p_anchor1 has hidden value 1 which never matches the query values 3 or 4 so anchor 1 contributes 0; anchor 2 at p_anchor2 has hidden value 2 which also never matches 3 or 4 so anchor 2 contributes 0. Therefore c_i equals (1 if bit i of (pos3 minus 1) is zero) plus (1 if bit i of (pos4 minus 1) is one). Classify by c_i: c_i equals 0 forces bit i of (pos3 minus 1) to be 1 and bit i of (pos4 minus 1) to be 0; c_i equals 2 forces bit i of (pos3 minus 1) to be 0 and bit i of (pos4 minus 1) to be 1; c_i equals 1 leaves those two bits equal but unpinned, push i into ambiguousBits34. Record determinedBits34 vector of length B with the determined bit values for pos3 minus 1 in determined positions and minus 1 in ambiguous positions.; NEW Phase 1D cleanup: build Cset3 as the vector of integers p in 1 through n such that for every i with determinedBits34 of i not equal to minus 1, bit i of (p minus 1) equals determinedBits34 of i, AND p is not equal to p_anchor1 AND p is not equal to p_anchor2. While size of Cset3 exceeds 1: take half equal to (size of Cset3 plus 1) divided by 2, let L be the first half elements of Cset3, build a set Lset for O of 1 lookup, build query q of length n plus 1 with q at p equal to 3 if p in L else q at p equal to 1; flush; read integer r. Anchor 1 contributes 1 because q at p_anchor1 equals 1 (since p_anchor1 not in L, as p_anchor1 not in Cset3) and hidden equals 1; anchor 2 contributes 0 because hidden equals 2 does not match q in 1 or 3; pos3 at unknown p3 in Cset3 contributes 1 if p3 in L; pos4 at unknown p4 contributes 0 because q at p4 is either 3 or 1, neither equals 4. So r minus 1 equals the indicator that pos3 is in L. Update Cset3 to L if indicator is 1 else to the elements of Cset3 not in Lset. When size of Cset3 reaches 1 set p_anchor3 equal to Cset3 of 0.; After Phase 1D compute D_mask_34 by OR ing 1 shifted left by i for every i with determinedBits34 of i not equal to minus 1. approach: triple-value joint Phase 2 binary search with disjoint partition separation
details: Keep Phase 1 unchanged (the chunked half-shifted-retry log-bit Phase 1 from 5b82d72). Replace the paired Phase 2 loop with a triple-value joint scheme. Process remaining values V in chunks of three (a,b,c). For each triple, maintain candidate sets Ca, Cb, Cc all initialized to the current global G of unlocated positions. Round 0 separation: partition G into three roughly equal disjoint parts P1, P2, P3 (sizes ceil(|G|/3), then halves of remainder). Build a query q of length n filled with v_anchor; for p in P1 set q[p]=a, for p in P2 set q[p]=b, for p in P3 set q[p]=c. Send query, receive r, let s = r - 1 (subtracting anchor's contribution). Each of a,b,c is in exactly one of P1/P2/P3, so the indicator vector (i_a, i_b, i_c) where i_x=1 iff x is in its chosen partition has sum s in 0..3. Cases: s=3 means Ca=P1, Cb=P2, Cc=P3 done. s=0 means none in chosen; for each value x in a,b,c do one extra query placing x in P2 only (rest=v_anchor), response minus 1 tells if x is in P2 (else P3 since P1 already excluded by s=0 logic for that value). Use at most 2 such follow-ups exploiting elimination. s=1 or s=2 (ambiguous): do up to two single-value localization queries (place a alone in P1, then b alone in P2, deduce c) to fully resolve which part each is in. Cap separation cost at 3 queries per triple. After separation Ca, Cb, Cc are disjoint subsets. Round k for k>=1: independent binary search per value, ordered round-robin. For value x with |Cx|>1, pick Sx = first half of Cx; query with q[p]=x for p in Sx and q[p]=v_anchor elsewhere; response minus 1 is 1 iff x in Sx; halve Cx accordingly. Continue until each Cx is a singleton. When |V| - idx is 1 or 2 at the end (leftover not forming a full triple), fall back to the existing paired or single-value binary search. After Phase 2 completes, the one remaining unassigned position takes value n by elimination as before. Edge case: if |G| < 3 at the start of a triple, skip to leftover handling. Edge case: when separating with s=0 and only 2 values remain to resolve, the second can be inferred by elimination, saving one query.
rationale: The paired Phase 2 approach has matured at 94.88 across multiple variants; processing three values per round aims to reduce per-value query cost by amortizing the joint partition query across three unknowns and opens a fresh Phase 2 direction distinct from the previously crashed quadruple variant.
